title.narrative: Church action for peaceful and democratic election

description.narrative:
2012 is an important year for East Timor as the young country will have a general election. East Timor has a history of conflict surrounding elections since it gained independence in 1999. For the upcoming election, CAFOD will make a small contribution to support CRS Timor Leste’s project to engage with the Church to support a peaceful election season in 2012. Learning from CRS’s prayer campaign around South Sudan’s secession, CRS have worked with the Justice and Peace Commission of Dili Diocese to develop a prayer campaign for Timor’s 2012 election season.
The key focus of the project, which is the 111 days of prayers and reflection, will start on February 22, 2012 “Ash Wednesday” until June 26, 2012 “Pentecost”.
The Church Action for Peaceful and Democratic Election (CAPADE Project) will utilise the Church’s vast network and great influence to call all citizens to refrain from violence and contribute to a peaceful election. This will be done through a mass prayer and reflection campaign, taking place daily and weekly at churches, during various congregations’ activities, at school, within youth groups and through the mass media. Peace promoters will help monitor and immediately report election-related incidents or conflicts to peace building institutions, in order to restrict small tensions escalating into full scale violent conflict.
